cohort.epv_flag: WARNING: M1 events-per-predictor = 7.91 (< 10). Coefficient estimates are variance-limited; treat individual hazard ratios as directional evidence, not precise effect sizes.

q1_lfp_adds_over_pressure.answer: The LFP block does not add detectable information beyond injury severity: cross-validated concordance rises from 0.583 (95% CI 0.518-0.651) with pressure alone to 0.574 (0.522-0.628) with pressure plus LFP, a change of -0.009 (95% CI -0.033 to +0.015), and the nested likelihood ratio test gives chi2(9) = 13.33, p = 0.148.

likelihood_ratio_test.note: Unpenalized stratified Cox fits. lfp_power_high_norm dropped from M1 as the compositional reference (the three normalized power bands sum to 1, so all three cannot be identified jointly without a penalty).

q2_direction_check.answer: The elastic net shrank all 4 mechanistic LFP coefficients to effectively zero (every |log HR| < 0.01, i.e. hazard ratios inside 0.99-1.01 per SD), so the penalized model retains no direction to check. In the unpenalized sensitivity fit, 2 of 4 point the WRONG way (lfp_variance_uV2 (HR 0.78 per SD, expected HR > 1), lfp_autocorr_lag1 (HR 0.98 per SD, expected HR > 1)), while lfp_ap_slope (HR 0.46 per SD, expected HR < 1), lfp_discharge_rate_per_min (HR 1.04 per SD, expected HR > 1) point as predicted.

table.rationale: Aperiodic exponent; flattening indexes a shift toward excitation in the excitation-inhibition balance, so a LOWER slope should predict a SHORTER latency to seizure (HR < 1 per unit slope).
Critical slowing indicator; variance rises as a network approaches instability, so HIGHER variance should predict a SHORTER latency (HR > 1).
Critical slowing indicator; lag-1 autocorrelation rises as recovery from perturbation slows near a bifurcation, so HIGHER autocorrelation should predict a SHORTER latency (HR > 1).
Interictal-like discharge rate; more spontaneous discharges indicate a more irritable network, so a HIGHER rate should predict a SHORTER latency (HR > 1).

q2_direction_check.note: A hazard ratio within 1% of 1.0 per SD is treated as carrying no direction. Reading the sign of a coefficient the penalty has already deleted would manufacture agreement out of rounding.

q3_critical_slowing_agreement.answer: The two critical slowing indicators were both shrunk out of the penalized model entirely, so the penalized fit cannot say whether they agree: lfp_variance_uV2 gives HR 1.00 per SD (1.00-1.00) and lfp_autocorr_lag1 gives HR 1.00 per SD (1.00-1.00), while the two features are themselves correlated at r = 0.67 (Spearman rho = 0.67, p = 2.08e-14) across larvae, so they do co-vary biologically even where the model declines to use them. In the unpenalized sensitivity fit they agree: lfp_variance_uV2 HR 0.78 per SD and lfp_autocorr_lag1 HR 0.98 per SD, both running counter to the critical slowing prediction, which points to a shared confound rather than a shared mechanism.

q4_within_stratum.answer: No: once the hit is held constant, the model cannot tell two larvae apart. Within-stratum concordance is 0.413 pair-weighted (chance is 0.500), and not one of the 4 drop-height strata has an interval excluding chance (per-stratum: 0 cm 0.163, 27 cm 0.528, 54 cm 0.522, 108 cm 0.430). Full within-stratum refits are reported but rest on only 19-25 events against up to 11 predictors, so they are descriptive rather than inferential.
q4_within_stratum.method_primary: within-stratum concordance of the global leave-one-fish-out risk score; only larvae from the same drop height are compared
q4_within_stratum.method_secondary: independent elastic-net refit inside each stratum, as specified

q5_injury_gradient.answer: Mean predicted susceptibility follows the injury gradient: the observed ordering is Sham < TBI_27cm < TBI_54cm < TBI_108cm (means -0.556, -0.064, +0.149, +0.491), against the expected sham < low < mid < high, with a monotone trend of Spearman rho = 0.947 (p = 4.23e-50) between drop height and risk score.
q5_injury_gradient.note: Risk score is the held-out Cox linear predictor; higher means higher hazard, i.e. shorter predicted latency.

q6_behaviour_vs_dose.answer: 3 of 3 baseline behavioural features are largely a restatement of injury dose (R^2 on max_pressure_kPa alone: beh_baseline_speed_mm_s 0.87, beh_baseline_immobile_frac 0.73, beh_baseline_burst_rate_per_min 0.85), leaving only 13%-27% of their variance independent of the hit.
q6_behaviour_vs_dose.premise_note: The stated premise is that injury suppresses locomotion. In this cohort baseline speed RISES with pressure (slope +0.00573 mm/s per kPa, r = 0.93), so the redundancy finding holds but the sign of the underlying relationship is opposite to the one assumed.

q7_leave_one_stratum_out.answer: No: transferred to an injury level it has never seen, the model is indistinguishable from chance in all 3 evaluable held-out strata (27 cm: c = 0.521 [0.368-0.692], 54 cm: c = 0.495 [0.356-0.646], 108 cm: c = 0.510 [0.379-0.651]), with every hyperparameter and scaling constant learned from the three training strata only. The 0 cm stratum could not be scored at all: every held-out larva received the same risk score (-0.9898); the retained predictors are constant within this stratum, so concordance is undefined rather than at chance.

q8_calibration.answer: Ranking is better than absolute timing: the calibration slope in the risk domain is 0.624 (95% CI 0.114-1.134, where 1.0 is perfect), while in the time domain regressing observed on predicted log-latency gives slope 0.240 and intercept 4.692, with predictions off by a median of 298 s and a mean signed bias of -110 s against a 1800 s observation window.
q8_calibration.time_domain_note: OLS of log(observed latency) on log(predicted median latency), events only. Slope 1 and intercept 0 would be perfect.

model_switch.note: Per-covariate flags: ['lfp_power_mid_norm']. The Weibull AFT fit is reported alongside as a sensitivity analysis only.

diagnostics.frailty_substitution: Requested: clutch_id as a frailty term. lifelines 0.30.3 provides no gamma-frailty Cox model, and its `cluster_col` sandwich estimator cannot be combined with `strata` (raises KeyError). Substitution applied and logged: clutch_id enters as a stratified baseline hazard (separate baseline seizure threshold per clutch), and all reported intervals use a clutch-level bootstrap so that the unit of resampling is the biological replicate, not the individual larva.

leakage_audit.description: Every FoldPipeline fit/predict pair is recorded. A violation is any prediction whose rows intersect its own training fold. See tests/test_leakage.py for the sentinel canary.
